clue.text: Originally NY was not the endless area of ramshackle housing

indicators.note: the letters are said to be in their original, unarranged form, so they must be rearranged to get the word they came from

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word 'the' is dropped

explanation.surface: A wistful remark that New York was once not the boundless metropolis it is now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' signals the anagram: NY, WAS, NOT and TH ('the' made 'endless' by losing its E) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of improvised shacks on a city's edge is exactly a slum settlement of this kind.

clue.text: It is omitted from printed translation. It's discriminating

indicators.note: is omitted from says the word 'it' must be taken out of the longer word that follows

parts.note: a subtitle is a translation printed on screen under a foreign film
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two terse sentences that read like a critic praising a translator's judgement in leaving a word out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine distinctions and nuanced perception: a discerning mind is called delicate or nuanced in this sense.

clue.text: Looks for acreage above Western Isles

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the first piece over the ones that follow

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for acre or acreage
aits (or eyots) are small islands in a river

explanation.surface: A surveyor scanning farmland lying above the Western Isles of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western Isles' suggests the Hebrides, but it splits into W and AITS, the small river islands of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: To look for something is to expect it or wait for it to arrive, a synonym.

clue.text: Capture steer in park that's buckled fencing over

indicators.note: fencing says one piece surrounds another like a fence round a field
something buckled is bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Rounding up a bullock in a park where the fencing has collapsed over the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckled' makes an anagram of STEER IN PARK, and 'fencing' wraps it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture an enemy soldier is to seize and detain him, the military phrase meaning exactly that.

clue.text: Drop in temperature — some corn's subdued

indicators.note: subdued means kept down, so in this down clue the corn piece sits beneath the first letter

parts.note: an ear is a head of corn, a portion of the crop

explanation.surface: A cold snap leaves the cornfield looking flattened and subdued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop in temperature' looks like one phrase, but 'Drop' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop is a single drop shed from the eye, so a drop of this kind is a synonym.

clue.text: Being upset, know-all, left out, urges: 'Tread warily'

indicators.note: being upset means being knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
left out says the letter L, for left, is omitted from the word before

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them, so eggs means urges

explanation.surface: A smug know-all, upset at being excluded, is advised to tread carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOWAL (know-all with one L 'left out') is the anagram 'Being upset', then EGGS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to proceed with great caution, as if any step might break something fragile.

clue.text: Note: a loud female can be vulgar

parts.note: f (forte) means loud in music

explanation.surface: A warning that a woman who talks loudly may come across as common.
explanation.walkthrough: NAFF is British slang for tacky or lacking style.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for tasteless or tacky, close to the sense of common or crude.

clue.text: Amorous relationship loses depth in marriage

indicators.note: loses says a letter is dropped from the word before

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual love affair

explanation.surface: A flirtation loses its intensity once the couple are wed.
explanation.definitionFit: A union or partnership; marriage was historically described as such a bond between families.

clue.text: Sport outfit embracing European style initially. It is most trendy

parts.note: sport means fun or amusement

indicators.note: embracing says the outfit word wraps around the letters that follow it

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothing, an outfit

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of style is used

explanation.surface: A sporty outfit with Continental flair is said to be the height of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Funky is slang for fashionable and stylish, so its superlative means the trendiest.

clue.text: Vetoes deliveries by jet

parts.note: jet black is a deep shade, so jet means black
in cricket a bowler's deliveries are balls

explanation.surface: Someone rejecting parcels sent by air.
explanation.walkthrough: In clubs, members voted against a candidate by putting a black ball in the ballot box.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude a candidate by secret negative vote is to reject or block him, a synonym.

clue.text: Pastry dish made from cut beef

indicators.note: cut says the last letter is chopped off the word

parts.note: flank is a cut of beef from the animal's side

explanation.surface: A savoury tart made with chopped beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut beef' looks like the filling; it is FLANK, a beef cut, itself 'cut' short.
explanation.definitionFit: An open pastry case with a filling is a tart, which is what this dish is.

clue.text: Personal development's part of my ideal, looking back. Expand it!

definitions.text: Personal development's part of my ideal, looking back. Expand it!

parts.words: Personal development's part of my ideal, looking back. Expand it!
parts.note: reading 'my ideal' backwards shows the three-letter abbreviation for home improvement work hidden inside it, and the clue asks for that abbreviation spelt out in full

explanation.surface: A self-help mantra: grow as a person and broaden your horizons.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, 'my ideal' hides DIY; 'Expand it!' asks for that abbreviation written out, so 'Personal development' means doing the work yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Home improvement work carried out by oneself rather than by paid tradesmen: personal development of one's property.

clue.text: Respites essential to recurrent dispute lessening

indicators.note: recurrent says the hidden letters are read backwards
essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Breaks are vital if an ongoing quarrel is to cool down.
explanation.definitionFit: Pauses or easings in pressure are respites, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Centre of exotic opal ground in volcano in SA

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
centre of says to drop the outer letters of the phrase and keep the inside

explanation.surface: A rare opal crushed inside a South American volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of' strips the end letters from EXOTIC OPAL to leave XOTICOPA, which is 'ground' into a volcano in Ecuador.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotopaxi is a famous active volcano in the Ecuadorian Andes, in South America.

clue.text: Pronounce a record player's music regularly acted out of sync

parts.note: a DJ (disc jockey) plays records

indicators.note: out of sync means disordered, so the letters are rearranged
regularly says every other letter of music is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disc jockey's set badly mistimed with the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes U and I from music; with ACTED they are rearranged 'out of sync' to UDICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a formal ruling or judgement is to pronounce on a matter, a synonym.

clue.text: Bows? What nonsense!

definitions.meaning: violin bows, playfully called the sticks for a fiddle
an old-fashioned exclamation of impatient disbelief

explanation.surface: Someone scoffing at a suggestion about bows.
explanation.definitionFit: The bows of violins are the sticks for a fiddle, and the same word is a dated exclamation of scorn.

clue.text: Island with gold male insect

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A man with gold on an island, like a castaway with treasure, and some bug.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH, a Scottish word for a small island, appears in place names like Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: A looper caterpillar is the larva of a moth, loosely called an insect.

clue.text: A continental fish in bottomless sea gets shelter

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the trimmed sea
bottomless says the last letter of sea, the bottom in a down clue, is dropped

parts.note: un is French for a
a shad is a fish of the herring family

explanation.surface: A European fish finds cover in the deep ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol or awning provides shelter from the sun's glare.

clue.text: Medical practitioner's sudden increase in new money acceptable

indicators.note: in says the sudden increase sits within the money phrase

parts.note: the euro is a currency
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'
a surge is a sudden increase

explanation.surface: A doctor gets an unexpected pay rise in the new currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain surgeon is a medical specialist, a kind of doctor or practitioner.

clue.text: Sculpture standing right out

indicators.note: out says the letter for right is removed

parts.note: stature means standing or reputation

explanation.surface: A carved figure standing outside to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' looks like part of the picture of the sculpture, but it is STATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved or cast figure of a person is a sculpture of this kind.

clue.text: Flying drones made hoarse noise

indicators.note: flying drones are scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drones in flight give off a harsh buzzing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper breathing noisily makes a rasping, hoarse sound through the nose.

clue.text: Anger returns in mad hasty display of wild emotion

indicators.note: in says the reversed anger word goes inside the rearranged letters
mad suggests crazily jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
returns says the word for anger is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Fury flares up again in a frenzied rush of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger' looks like part of the emotion on display; 'returns' turns it round, and 'in' puts that inside HYSTA, which 'mad' makes of 'hasty'.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncontrollable outburst of emotion or panic is what hysteria describes.

clue.text: Frenchman's brother going to posh school

parts.note: Eton is England's best-known exclusive public school

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's brother is off to an expensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite private boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Brittany, the region of north-west France, is a Frenchman.

clue.text: Money's genuine

definitions.meaning: the currency of Brazil, and an old Spanish silver coin

explanation.surface: Someone vouches that the cash is not counterfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the Brazilian unit of currency and an adjective for authentic.

clue.text: Shape of ground?

explanation.surface: A question about the outline of a plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a Test cricket ground in Kennington, London, and is itself egg-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: An elongated round outline describes a sports arena's typical form and also names one.

clue.text: He leads most of group with energy to me in this instance

indicators.note: most of says the final letter of the group word is dropped

parts.note: a pack is a group
the person writing this clue is the crossword compiler

explanation.surface: A self-portrait of someone at the front of a group, with the narrator joining in energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me in this instance' is the compiler referring to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who sets the speed at the front of a race is the one in the lead.

clue.text: Look small-minded in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: mean means petty or small-minded

explanation.surface: Someone whose talk reveals them as petty.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing or facial expression is their appearance, or look.

clue.text: Nuclear site's diesel spilled around westward slope

indicators.note: around says the scrambled fuel letters go round the reversed slope
spilled means scattered, so the letters are rearranged
westward in an across clue means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: a fall is a downward slope

explanation.surface: A fuel spill on a hillside near a nuclear plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westward' turns the slope round to LLAF, and 'around' puts SEIELD ('spilled' fuel) round it. Sellafield is the nuclear plant on the Cumbrian coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sellafield is the major nuclear reprocessing plant on the Cumbrian coast of north-west England.
